name: Joyanta Jyoti Mondal
summary: AI/ML researcher with 5+ years of academic and applied experience in deep learning, model optimization, and computer vision for healthcare and social impact. Demonstrated expertise in designing parameter-efficient neural architectures for resource-constrained, real-world domains, spanning interdisciplinary projects in both academic and applied settings. Recognized with multiple academic honors, prestigious grants, and fellowships, with a commitment to translating AI research into reliable, and practical applications.

Graduate Teaching Assistant @ University: Delivered individualized feedback and guidance to 145+ students in Data Structures, improving assignment quality and overall course performance by ensuring weekly one-on-one consultations.
Research & Teaching Assistant @ BRAC Uni: Developed an efficient Deep CNN architecture for detecting Air Quality Index (AQI), reducing prediction error by up to 78% compared to state-of-the-art models with an R² value of 0.39, enabling near real-time and offline air quality monitoring.
Guided a research project on a fog-resilient Bangla license plate recognition system integrating Dark Channel Prior and YOLOv8, achieving 98.5% detection accuracy in adverse weather.
Mentored 120+ students through assignment reviews and weekly consultations, improving capstone project deliverables and technical competency.
Undergraduate Research Assistant @ BRAC: Created a 1,200+ image dataset and testbed to evaluate Progressive JPEG retrieval system under real-world bandwidth limits, achieving up to 69% faster load times and 27% compressed size in cloud applications, served over 1 Million users.

Led a project on detecting plant diseases using a lightweight DCNN architecture, achieving 98% accuracy, using 93.07% fewer computational parameters than the average of state-of-the-art architectures.
Improved document keyword extraction using a pre-trained BERT model in a cloud system, maintaining a consistent low query time (54–58ms) for high-throughput environments.
